Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Putting a short, actionable summary below and attaching a simple residency map + current subprocessor roster. Karthik is looped in for technical details on deletion and encryption. Marissa is on the thread for commercial questions (EU-only pricing / Dedicated vs Private).

Quick summary (hosted offering):
- Regions: Redwood hosts inference endpoints in the following public regions: US East (us-east-1), US West (us-west-2), EU (eu-west-1). We also have edge exits in APAC (asia-southeast1) for reduced latency when customers select that region.
- Routing/hops: Customer requests are received by the public API gateway in the selected region; the serving runtime executes on GPUs in that region. Control-plane metadata (routing decisions, metrics) may traverse our central control plane for orchestration; payloads are not stored long-term in the control plane. The attached "residency_map_v1.pdf" visualizes typical request flow and transient hops.
- Subprocessors (high level): AWS (hosting in US & EU), GCP (APAC edge), Fastly/Cloud CDN (edge network), Datadog (metrics/ops), HashiCorp Vault / AWS KMS for key management. See the attached CSV for full roster.
- Retention defaults: request payloads (text prompts) are retained in encrypted transient stores for up to 30 days by default for debugging and quality monitoring; embeddings are retained 90 days by default unless configured otherwise. Audit logs and token-level billing records are kept for 365 days.
- Deletion process: customers can request immediate deletion via the Console or API (DELETE /v1/records/{id}). Upon request we mark records for deletion (tombstone) and background purge jobs run across storage tiers. For hosted customers we commit to completing physical data removal from primary stores within 72 hours of the deletion request; final removal from backups and replicated caches can take up to 30 days depending on the tier. For Dedicated/Private deployments, the same APIs trigger in-customer infrastructure and removal accelerates per the environment SLA.
- Controls: All payloads are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). KMS/HSM keys are supported for Dedicated/Private customers; for hosted customers we offer a customer-managed key option in our enterprise plan.

Attachments: residency_map_v1.pdf, subprocessor_roster_20260610.csv (both attached to this thread).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review the attached map/roster and tell us if you want an "EU-only execution" playbook — we can spin up a scoped EU-only tenant for the POC.
2) If you need SOC2 artifacts, I can share a secure link (we'll need an NDA for full evidence).

Karthik — can you add a short note on the actual purge mechanics for ephemeral KV caches and backups?

Best,

Hi Alice — quick technical clarifications to complement Jonas' summary: 

1) Execution locality: The serving runtime is pinned to the GPU pool in the chosen region for the session. For multi-stage flows that call external tooling, payloads are only forwarded to additional services when explicitly configured (e.g., function/tool calls). 

2) Transient caches (KV/cache): We use in-memory and short-lived on-disk caches for KV cache and prefix caching. Those caches are cleared on process restart; when a customer requests deletion we invalidate relevant keys immediately and schedule any on-disk cached shards for purge. For hosted customers: immediate invalidation -> background wipe -> confirmation when the purge job completes (we return an API confirmation ID you can track).

3) Backups & replication: Nightly backups are incremental and encrypted. We have a 30-day retention window for backups by default; deletion requests generate a tombstone that prevents restoration of purged objects, and we tie that into our backup retention automation. Complete removal from long-term archival stores can take up to 30 days.

4) Subprocessor specifics: 
- AWS: compute/storage in US/EU regions we listed.
- GCP: edge routing nodes in APAC (no primary model execution unless customer is on a specific APAC tenant).
- Fastly: CDN/edge for streaming & websockets.
- Datadog/Sentry: telemetry (we can disable telemetry forwarding by contract).

5) Evidence and attestations: SOC2 Type II summary and control matrix are available via our secure evidence portal (we will provide a link after we get an executed NDA). For procurement questionnaires, we can provide a pre-filled vendor spreadsheet that maps our controls to their questions.

If you prefer an EU-only trajectory for the POC, our recommended path is: EU-only hosted tenant (no APAC exits), customer-managed key (if required), and a scoped subprocessor addendum. That combination minimizes cross-border exports.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call with your security team to walk the map.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Applied Security — Redwood Inference
